scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-01.statement: Field route completion rate for manual-read accounts was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for the Aug-Sep 2026 period, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: 1240 disputed bills were on ESTIMATED reads per billing-db.

F-03.statement: 1785 disputed bills were on ACTUAL reads per billing-db.

F-04.statement: billing-db.tariff_change_log shows 0 tariff change records for the review period.

F-05.statement: CRM dispute response times for the review period: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets.

F-07.statement: route-log.lagging_routes lists 14 routes with distinct completion values; sample record shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: Of 1240 AMI read events tied to disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 arrived before cutoff and were exported but rejected on billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while 56 had no read received and were not exported.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: Dispute volume is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem that an AI auto-answer agent can resolve, independent of whether bills themselves are wrong.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused systematic bill errors (e.g. incorrect estimate substitution or acceptance logic), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-FAILURE.statement: AMI interval reads are failing to arrive or validate correctly via the nightly MDMS export, forcing more estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: The manual meter-read daily upload from the field contractor is failing or degrading (missed/invalid reads), causing estimate substitution and billing errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: MeterWorks field staffing shortfalls reduced route completion rates, increasing estimated (non-actual) bills and disputes.

H-USAGE-INCREASE-BILL-SHOCK.statement: Bills are accurate but reflect a real rise in consumption/charges, and disputes are 'bill shock' complaints rather than evidence of billing errors.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-IMPORT-REJE.statement: Billing import rejects AMI reads flagged with a REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION status even when the read arrived before cutoff and was exported, forcing estimate substitution for otherwise valid, timely reads.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, with 9,200 manual-read accounts in scope; this shows manual meter-reading routes were under-completed in the surge period, which is a plausible contributor to increased estimate substitution for those accounts.

E-01's observation still shows field route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9,200 manual-read accounts for Aug-Sep 2026 — that metric is unchanged. It no longer supports PR-ROOT/PR-CHAIN-3/PR-A-ESTIMATED-DISPUTES-ROUTE-LIN's inference that this under-completion materially drives the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, since E-11 shows 95.5% of those bills had a valid pre-cutoff AMI read rejected on billing import, not an absent read from route non-completion.

Of disputed bills broken down by read type, 1785 were on ACTUAL reads and 1240 on ESTIMATED reads, so a majority (about 59%) of disputed bills were not estimate-substituted at all. This means estimate-substitution-driven causes (AMI export failures, field manual-read handoff failures) can at best explain a minority of the dispute surge.

E-02's counts still stand unchanged: 1240 disputed bills on ESTIMATED reads and 1785 on ACTUAL reads. It no longer supports PR-A-ESTIMATED-DISPUTES-ROUTE-LIN's framing that the 1240 ESTIMATED-read bills are plausibly tied to field route under-completion, since E-11 shows that same ESTIMATED population is overwhelmingly explained by AMI reads rejected on billing import, not manual-read non-delivery.
billing-db's tariff change log shows zero tariff changes on record, so no rate/tariff adjustment occurred that could explain higher charges on bills during the dispute surge period.

crm-tickets reports 2440 dispute tickets in the review period with median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA. Response handling is currently meeting its SLA, so the ticket backlog/response-speed is not an unmet performance gap at present.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; this is a stakeholder claim, not independent evidence, and it echoes the already-recorded tool finding (E-03: 0 tariff changes Aug-Sep), adding corroboration but no new scope or authority.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims the manual-read workforce has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those accounts to receive estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a causal mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already observed in E-01, but SH-FIELD has a disclosed bias toward attributing problems to staffing and seeking headcount increases.

E-06's stakeholder claim — a three-reader shortfall since July causing late routes and estimated bills — still stands as an unverified claim about staffing and route timing. It no longer plausibly explains the mechanism behind the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, since E-11 shows 95.5% of those bills had a valid, timely AMI read that was rejected by a billing-import rule rather than being left without any accepted read due to late manual routes.

crm-tickets' monthly dispute volume log shows tickets stable near 600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 (610, 590) then jumping to 1180 in Aug and 1260 in Sep, confirming the timing and roughly-doubled magnitude of the surge that triggered the initial request (CL-01), and showing the surge continued/grew into September rather than being a single-month blip. The Aug+Sep total (2440) matches the ticket count in E-04's response-time dataset, confirming that measurement covers the surge period itself.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms that utility-requested route priority changes are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation, corroborating the already-recorded K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement for push_route_update rather than revealing a new causal fact.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes identifies 14 distinct routes currently behind schedule, each with its own completion value; the sample route R-00 sits at 0.70 completion, below the 0.95 target and below the Aug-Sep aggregate 0.88 (E-01). This gives route-level granularity on the under-completion already captured in F-01 but does not by itself identify a cause (staffing vs. handoff vs. other) for why these specific routes lag.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message, vendor ticket TX-4471) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned as of today, meaning the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query path may now be executable. This does not itself provide any AMI read-event data or confirm/refute AMI-side failure; it only concerns access status, not the content of the AMI read log.

E-11 shows that of the AMI read events behind the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read arrive before cutoff and get exported to billing, but billing import rejected them with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution; only 56 (4.5%) had genuinely no read received. This means the dominant driver of estimated-read disputes is a billing-import rejection rule acting on otherwise-valid high-consumption AMI reads, not AMI read non-delivery, and not (for this AMI-channel population) field route under-completion.

U-MAJORITY-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What causes the majority of disputed bills that are on ACTUAL reads (59%, F-03) rather than estimated ones, e.g. a billing import validation rule change (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE)?
U-MAJORITY-DISPUTE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation should target billing import/validation rules (DA-RULES) rather than field staffing/route fixes; without it, SC-ROOT-CAUSE-IDENTIFIED cannot be met and any 'fix wrong bills' automation would target the wrong mechanism.
U-MAJORITY-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Review billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) for changes around Aug 2026 correlated with ACTUAL-read disputes; cross-check billing-db import validation status for the same accounts.
U-MAJORITY-DISPUTE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Do not scope or build any automated remediation (e.g. billing-rule fix or AI auto-fix) until the DA-RULES review identifies the mechanism; SC-ROOT-CAUSE-IDENTIFIED remains unmet in the interim.

U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Does the vendor-provisioned MDMS export, currently blocked (mdms-export DEGRADED, ACCESS_PENDING per the latest recovery decision), hide AMI read failures that also contribute to estimate substitution?
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: If AMI/MDMS read failures are also contributing, remediation scope must include the AMI vendor path, not just field manual reads; this cannot currently be assessed while mdms-export is DEGRADED.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Request Telemetrix (ORG-AMI) to provision mdms-export access (currently ACCESS_PENDING); once HEALTHY, review the AMI read event log (DA-MDMS) for the Aug-Sep period.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Treat H-AMI-DATA-FAILURE as an open candidate mechanism, neither confirmed nor ruled out, while mdms-export remains DEGRADED.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: Now that MDMS export access is provisioned, E-11 shows the blocked export was not primarily hiding AMI read non-delivery (only 56/1240, 4.5%); the dominant factor is billing import rejecting valid high-consumption AMI reads (1184/1240, 95.5%).

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VALIDIT.question: Is the field reader shortfall genuinely three staff since July, or does SH-FIELD's staffing-headcount incentive bias this attribution of the route-completion shortfall?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VALIDIT.decision_impact: If the staffing shortfall is overstated or not the true driver of the route-completion gap, recommending contract headcount changes would be premature and E-06 should not be treated as corroborating causation.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VALIDIT.resolution_path: Cross-check SH-FIELD's self-reported staffing shortfall (E-06) against MeterWorks contractor timesheets or headcount records independent of SH-FIELD's own interview.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VALIDIT.safe_placeholder: Treat the staffing-shortage mechanism (H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE) as plausible but unverified; do not approve a contract headcount increase on E-06 alone.

U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDI.question: Could ticket volume return to baseline via ticket deflection/auto-closure (e.g. an AI auto-answer agent) without underlying bill correctness improving, masking the true problem?
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDI.decision_impact: If an auto-answer/ticket-deflection feature could lower monthly dispute volume without fixing bill correctness, SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE alone would be a false success signal.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDI.resolution_path: When evaluating dispute-volume trend, pair it with the ACTUAL vs ESTIMATED read-type breakdown and root-cause findings for the same months to confirm any drop reflects fewer wrong bills, not deflection.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDI.safe_placeholder: Do not treat dispute-ticket volume alone as proof of resolution; any ticket-closure feature must be paired with the estimated-read dispute-share and root-cause metrics before declaring success.

U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALID.question: Does the daily manual-read upload handoff (H-FIELD-BILL, delivery_status and semantic_validity both UNKNOWN) deliver and validate correctly, or could handoff failure - independent of staffing - account for part of the route-completion/estimate-substitution gap?
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALID.decision_impact: If H-FIELD-BILL itself is degraded, part of the route-completion shortfall (E-01) could stem from upload-handoff failure rather than staffing (E-06), changing where remediation should target.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALID.resolution_path: Obtain H-FIELD-BILL delivery_status/semantic_validity logs from ORG-FIELD for Aug-Sep 2026 and compare against route-log completion records.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALID.safe_placeholder: Continue using route-log completion rate (E-01) as the operative field-read gap measure; do not attribute the gap solely to staffing or solely to handoff failure until logs are reviewed.

A-STAFFING-CLAIM-CORROBORATION.statement: The reported field reader shortfall (E-06) is treated as a probable contributor to the measured route-completion shortfall (E-01), though E-06 is an unverified, bias-prone stakeholder claim (SH-FIELD has a disclosed headcount incentive).

A-ESTIMATED-DISPUTES-ROUTE-LIN.statement: The 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-02) are assumed to substantially overlap with the 9,200 under-completed manual-read accounts (E-01) rather than AMI-side estimate substitution, since MDMS/AMI export access is currently blocked.

A-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT.statement: The disputed-bill read-type breakdown (E-02, 3025 bills) is assumed to be drawn from the same Aug-Sep review period as ticket volume (E-07) and the SLA dataset (E-04, 2440 tickets), despite the differing counts.
